paragraphs: We provide brands, retailers and other clients a holistic view of consumer shopping behavior globally to drive mission-critical strategic and operating decisions and facilitate better economic outcomes.

We are a leading global consumer intelligence company positioned at the nexus of brands, retailers and consumers. We manage a comprehensive and integrated ecosystem – The NIQ Ecosystem – which combines proprietary data, best-in-class technology, human intelligence and highly sophisticated software applications and analytics solutions (the "Ecosystem" or "The NIQ Ecosystem"). Our unified, artificial intelligence ("AI") and machine learning powered technology platform aggregates, harmonizes and enriches vast amounts of global consumer shopping data from a myriad of diverse sources, generates rich, proprietary reference data and metadata and provides a global, omnichannel view of consumer shopping behavior – The Full ViewTM.

Our global reach spans 90 countries, covering approximately 82% of the world's population, more than half of global gross domestic product ("GDP") and more than $7.4 trillion in global consumer spend as of December 31, 2025. Leveraging our strong NIQ brand, long-term client relationships, global scale, proprietary technology and extensive data and insights, we are positioned as a global leader in measuring, analyzing and predicting consumer behavior in the FMCG vertical, T&D and other verticals in which we operate. Our solutions, mission-critical insights, analytics and software applications are deeply embedded across our clients' enterprise supporting their strategic and operational decisions, enabling them to measure performance, maintain and strengthen their market positions and drive innovation and profitable growth.

Global consumer spend is estimated at $65 trillion during 2025. Within this expansive economy, the consumer shopping landscape is rapidly changing, creating strategic and operational challenges, as well as growth opportunities for brands, retailers and other industry participants. Consumer purchase patterns have become increasingly "omnichannel" with consumers shopping across a growing number of platforms and channels including brick-and-mortar stores, online and mobile platforms and social-commerce and quick-commerce channels. This rapidly changing consumer shopping "journey" has significantly increased the volume and complexity of shopping and transaction data. Simultaneously, consumers are increasingly seeking a more convenient and personalized shopping experience which amplifies competition among the growing number of consumer brands and shopping channels.

We believe this dynamic, omnichannel, highly competitive backdrop creates significant growth opportunities for The NIQ Ecosystem. Companies increasingly seek real-time access to trusted, neutral, comprehensive and granular intelligence and analytics, as well as appropriate data governance, that enables them to efficiently engage consumers, drive sales, increase repeat purchases and foster loyalty across global markets, which we believe can only be accomplished with NIQ's global, mission-critical view of consumer shopping behavior. We obtain data on online and offline consumer shopping behavior from diverse sources including retail point-of-sale feeds, global consumer shopping receipts, panels of more than 5.5 million consumers in more than 50 countries and direct partnerships with leading eCommerce players, covering a total of approximately 18 million consumer relationships. We also generate substantial amounts of proprietary data such as insights at specific store and consumer levels and evidence-based recommendations that support our clients' growth strategies.

Since March 2021, we have invested approximately $400 million to transform our Ecosystem and enhance our technology platform. We leverage a long history of proprietary knowledge and advanced AI and machine learning techniques for multiple use cases, from ingesting and standardizing data faster and more accurately, to creating significant amounts of granular reference data and metadata, to creating new tools within our software applications and analytics on consumer preferences and shopping trends. Our investment, development and use of AI across our platform enables clients to make better decisions and benefit from a better experience. For example, in 2024, we launched our generative AI tool, Ask Arthur, which is currently utilized by our clients to quickly find information, interpret data, onboard and train new analysts and make informed business decisions.
Our solutions align to two product groupings: (1) Intelligence and (2) Activation.

•Intelligence offerings are comprised of omnichannel measurement, consumer behavior and insights and retailer solutions, which are utilized by both consumer brands and retailer clients. These products help clients to measure their market share of consumer purchases across channels, helping them understand the "what," "where," "who" and "how much"—what the consumer bought, who the consumer is, where they shopped and how much they bought. Clients can see their market share by product, by market and by channel, sales volume movements across those same dimensions and pricing and promotion trends. Intelligence accounted for approximately 81% of our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 and is generally sold through multi-year or annual subscription contracts.

•Activation offerings are comprised of innovation, brand and media and analytics products that provide clients with insights about "why" consumers made a certain purchase, guide clients on "what to do next" and "who to target" around new product introduction and innovation, pricing, promotion strategy, targeted advertising and other drivers of growth. Leveraging our highly granular unified data and technology platform, our Activation offerings include custom, predictive analytics and reports that our clients use to optimize brand and trade decisions as well as new product testing. Activation accounted for approximately 19% of our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025. For the year ended December 31, 2025, approximately 73% of our Activation revenue was highly reoccurring revenue, meaning revenue from either annual, multi-year contracts or from a client purchasing the same solution in the same country each year for the past three years. Activation solutions also present significant cross-selling opportunities, as approximately 78% of Activation revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 came from existing Intelligence clients, while approximately 40% of our Intelligence large and mid-sized clients have purchased Activation solutions, representing an attractive opportunity to increase penetration.

The scale, breadth and depth of our data, combined with our deep industry knowledge, scalable AI-powered technology platform and strong global relationships enables us to provide relevant solutions to brands, retailers, other companies and government entities. Our diverse client base of approximately 23,000 companies spans industries and geographies. We work with many of the world's largest consumer brands and retailers – including approximately half of the Fortune 500 and nearly 80% of the Fortune 100 companies—as well as clients in high-growth verticals and SMB.

Our solutions enable executives, sales leaders, marketers, category management teams, media leaders and research and development teams to drive mission-critical strategic and operating decisions that span our clients' enterprise, including:
•measuring and assessing omnichannel sales performance across markets to provide visibility on which products are sold, who buys them, why, where and how;
•optimizing pricing and promotion to evaluate the impact on sales;
•segmenting and personalizing consumer products and experiences to drive sales conversion and repeat purchases across channels;

headings: Risks Related to our Business and Operations
1. We derive a significant portion of our revenues from sales of our subscription-based products. If our clients terminate or fail to renew their subscriptions, our business could suffer.
4. If we are not able to maintain consumer panels of sufficient size and scope, or if the costs of establishing and maintaining our panels increase, our business could be harmed.
5. If we are unsuccessful at investing in growth opportunities, our business could be materially and adversely affected.
6. Macroeconomic factors could continue to adversely affect our business and financial results.

7. The market for consumer measurement and business solutions products and services is highly competitive; if we cannot compete effectively, our revenues could decline and our business could be harmed.
8. Consolidation in the industries in which our clients operate could put pressure on the pricing of our services, thereby leading to decreased earnings and cash flows.

9. If sources from which we obtain information limit our access to such information or institute or increase fees for accessing such information, our business could be materially and adversely harmed.
10. A loss or decrease in business of one or more of our largest clients could adversely impact our business, results of operations and financial condition.
11. We face risks related to sales to government entities.
12. Our ability to successfully manage ongoing organizational changes and growth could impact our business results.
13. We may not fully realize the anticipated benefits of our completed or future combinations, acquisitions, joint ventures and strategic investments, which may expose us to additional risks.
14. If we are unable to attract, retain and engage employees, we may not be able to compete effectively and will not be able to expand our business.
15. Inadequacy of our insurance coverage or an inability to procure contractually required coverage could adversely affect our business.
16. Natural disasters, geo-political events and other highly disruptive events could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

17. Because we generally recognize revenue ratably over the term of each subscription agreement, downturns or upturns in our sales may not be immediately reflected in our financial condition and results of operations.
18. If we fail to maintain and enhance our brand, our ability to expand our client base may be impaired and our business, financial condition and results of operations may suffer.

paragraphs: Investing in our ordinary shares involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the risks and uncertainties described below together with all of the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our consolidated financial statements and the related notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, before deciding to invest in our ordinary shares. If any of the following risks should occur, our business, prospects, operating results and financial condition could suffer materially, the trading price of our ordinary shares could decline and you could lose all or part of your investment. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties that we are unaware of or that we do not currently deem material may also become important factors that adversely affect our business.

We currently derive a significant portion of our revenues from long-term subscription contracts, which are typically two-to-five years in duration. This has generally provided us with revenue that is recurring in nature due to high renewal rates among our clients, as demonstrated by our net dollar retention rates. If clients terminate their subscriptions for our products, do not renew their subscriptions, delay renewals of their subscriptions or renew on terms less favorable to us, our revenues could decline and our business could suffer.

Our clients have no obligation to renew after the expiration of their initial subscription period, and current subscriptions may not be renewed at the same or higher dollar amounts, if at all. Our client renewal rates may decline or fluctuate due to a number of factors, including client dissatisfaction with our products, the costs or functionality of our products, the prices or functionality of products offered by our competitors, the health of the consumer data measurement marketplace and the industries in which we operate, mergers and acquisitions affecting our client base and general economic conditions or reductions in our clients' spending levels. If our clients do not renew their agreements, require pricing concessions, terminate their agreements, renew their agreements on terms less favorable to us or fail to license additional product subscriptions, our revenue may decline, and as a result our business, results of operations and financial condition could be adversely affected.

In addition, as our products evolve and competitors introduce lower cost or differentiated products that are perceived to compete with our products and services, our ability to license subscriptions for our products could be impaired. Similarly, our subscription revenue could be adversely affected if clients perceive that features incorporated into competitive products reduce the need for our products or if they prefer to purchase other products that are bundled with products offered by other companies that operate in adjacent markets and compete with our products. In addition, the value of our products and services to our clients depends, in part, on our clients' ability to use them as part of an overall effective marketing strategy and as permitted by regulations related to data subject consent.

2. We rely on third parties to provide certain data, services and information technology and operations functions in connection with the provision of our current products and services. The loss or limitation of access to that data, or to those services or functions, could harm our ability to provide our products and services.

We rely on third parties, including retailers, panelists and other third parties, to provide data, services and information technology and operations functions for use in connection with the provision of our current products and services, and our reliance on third-party providers is growing. For example, we enter into agreements with third parties to obtain data from which we create products and services and we recruit panelists to provide data from which we create products and services. We also obtain certain data from data sharing arrangements with companies who may compete with us. These suppliers of data may increase restrictions on our use of such data due to factors such as heightened regulations related to consumer privacy, cybersecurity risk and failure to adhere to our or their quality control standards or otherwise satisfactorily perform services. Third-party data providers may also increase the prices they charge for data or the terms under which they provide us data or refuse altogether to license the data to us (in some cases because of exclusive agreements they may have entered into with our competitors). In the event that such data and services are unavailable for our use or the cost of acquiring such data increases, or such third-party data provider refuses to provide data, or fails to deliver data to us, our ability to provide products and services to our clients may be adversely impacted, and as a result our business, results of operations and financial condition could be adversely affected.

paragraphs: On July 22, 2025, the Reorganization was completed, whereby NIQ Global Intelligence plc became the direct parent of AI PAVE and the indirect parent of other intermediate holding companies, including Intermediate Dutch Holdings B.V., a private company with limited liability organized under the laws of the Netherlands ("Dutch Holdings"). All holders of equity interests in AI PAVE became shareholders of NIQ Global Intelligence plc.

On July 24, 2025, we completed our IPO, in which we issued and sold 50,000,000 ordinary shares at the initial public offering price of $21.00 per share. We received aggregate net proceeds of $985.1 million after deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and estimated offering expenses payable by us. The aggregate net proceeds were used to repay a portion of the Company's outstanding borrowings. See Note 1. "Organization" and Note 10. "Debt" in our notes to the consolidated financial statements for additional information.

On July 11, 2025, the Credit Agreement was amended, subject to the closing of the IPO, to, among other things, (i) increase the aggregate principal amount of the Revolver to $750.0 million, (ii) extend the maturity date with respect to the Revolver to July 30, 2030; provided that if by a date no later than the Modified Maturity Date (as defined below), any term loans borrowed under the Credit Agreement with an aggregate principal amount in excess of $1.0 billion are outstanding and the maturity date applicable to such term loans is earlier than the date that is 90 days after July 30, 2030 (the "Trigger Maturity Date"), such maturity date shall be the date that is 91 days prior to the Trigger Maturity Date (the "Modified Maturity Date"), (iii) reduce the interest rate spread with respect to the revolving facility to a spread of 225 to 275 basis points dependent on certain ratio levels and (iv) reduce the commitment fee rate with respect to the Revolver to 25 to 37.5 basis points dependent on certain ratio levels.

On August 12, 2025, the Credit Agreement was amended to, among other things, (a) refinance and replace the existing USD Term Loan with a new USD term loan facility with a reduced interest rate spread of 225 to 250 basis points dependent on certain ratio levels, (b) refinance and replace the existing EUR Term Loan with a new EUR term loan facility with a reduced interest rate spread of 275 to 300 basis points dependent on certain ratio levels, (c) extend the maturity date with respect to the USD and EUR term loan facilities to October 31, 2030 and (d) reduce the interest rate spread with respect to the Revolver to a spread of 175 to 225 basis points dependent on certain ratio levels. See Note 10. "Debt" in our notes to the consolidated financial statements for additional information.

On April 21, 2025, we completed the Gastrograph Acquisition for cash consideration of $12.5 million, subject to certain working capital adjustments. We accounted for the transaction as an asset acquisition as substantially all of the fair value of the assets acquired was concentrated in Gastrograph's developed technology, which includes applications, models and the underlying database. We believe the Gastrograph Acquisition further strengthens our AI capabilities and competitive differentiation to provide consumer packaged goods companies with The Full ViewTM.

On July 10, 2025, we entered into a definitive agreement to acquire 100% of the share capital of M-Trix, a data intelligence and market analytics company based in Brazil. The transaction closed on August 1, 2025 for total cash consideration of approximately BRL340.0 million (equivalent to approximately $54.2 million USD), subject to customary purchase price adjustments, of which only BRL150.0 million (equivalent to approximately $26.8 million USD) was paid upon the closing.

The remaining BRL190.0 million will be paid as follows: (i) BRL60.0 million upon the first anniversary of the closing, (ii) BRL BRL60.0 million upon the second anniversary of the closing, (iii) BRL50.0 million upon the third anniversary of the closing and (iv) BRL20.0 million following the sixth anniversary of the closing, subject to any ongoing claims for which M-Trix is held indemnifiable. Only the Holdback Amount will be subject to adjustment by the the Interbank Deposit Certificate of Brazil ("CDI").

In connection with the acquisition of M-Trix, we entered into a credit agreement with Banco J.P. Morgan S.A. on July 28, 2025, whereby we received BRL150.0 million (equivalent to approximately $26.8 million USD) to finance the transaction. The BRL Loan is subject to interest at the CDI rate plus a spread of 280 basis points. We settled the BRL Loan, including the accrued interest, during the third quarter of 2025.

We believe the acquisition will expand our presence in Latin America and allow for enhancements to our existing offerings. The acquisition was accounted for as a business combination using the acquisition method. See Note 3. "Acquisitions" in our notes to the consolidated financial statements for additional information.

paragraphs: 本公司為品牌、零售商及其他客戶提供全球消費購物行為的整體視圖，以推動關鍵性的戰略與運營決策，並促進更好的經濟成果。

本公司為全球領先的消費者智慧公司，處於品牌、零售商與消費者之間的交點。我們管理一個全面且整合的生態系統 – The NIQ Ecosystem – 這個生態系統結合了專屬資料、最佳級技術、人類智慧與高度先進的軟體應用與分析解決方案（簡稱 "Ecosystem" 或 "The NIQ Ecosystem"）。我們的統一、以人工智慧（"AI"）與機器學習為動力的技術平台，整合、協調並豐富來自多樣化來源的全球消費購物資料，產生豐富的專屬參考資料與元資料，並提供全球、跨通路的消費購物行為視圖 – The Full ViewTM。

全球消費支出預估在 2025 年達到 65 兆美元。在這廣大的經濟體中，消費者購物的景觀正快速變化，為品牌、零售商及其他產業參與者帶來戰略與運營的挑戰，以及成長機會。消費者購買新型態已逐漸趨向 "全通路"，消費者透過越來越多的平台與通路進行購物，包括實體店面、線上與行動平台，以及社交 commerce 與即時 commerce 通路。這快速變化的消費者購物 "旅程"，已大幅增加購物與交易資料的體積與複雜性。同時，消費者正 increasingly 尋求更便利且個性化的購物體驗，這也加劇了眾多消費者品牌與購物通路之間的競爭。

我們認為這個動態、跨通路、高度競爭的背景，為 The NIQ Ecosystem 創造了顯著的成長機會。企業 increasingly 尋求即時取得受信任、中立、全面且細緻的智慧與分析，以及適當的資料治理，以有效與消費者互動、推動銷售、增加重複購買與培育忠誠度，這一點我們認為唯有 NIQ 提供的全球、關鍵性消費購物行為視圖才能實現。我們從多樣化的來源取得線上與線下消費購物行為資料，包括零售點銷售資料流、全球消費購物收據、超過 5.5 百萬名消費者在超過 50 個國家的調查樣本，以及與領先電商業者的直接合作夥伴關係，涵蓋總計約 18 百萬名消費者關係。我們也產生大量專屬資料，例如特定商店與消費者層面的洞察，以及基於證據的建議，以支援客戶的成長策略。

自 2021 年 3 月起，我們已投資約 400 百萬美元，以轉型我們的 Ecosystem 並強化我們的技術平台。我們運用長期的專屬知識與先進的 AI 與機器學習技術，應用於多種用途，從更快更準確地吸收與標準化資料，到產生大量細緻的參考資料與元資料，再到在軟體應用與分析中創造新的工具，以瞭解消費者偏好與購物趨勢。我們在平台上的投資、開發與 AI 使用，使客戶能做出更好的決策並享有更好的體驗。例如，在 2024 年，我們推出了我們的生成式 AI 工具 Ask Arthur，目前被客戶用來快速尋找資訊、解讀資料、上手與培訓新分析師，並做出明智的商業決策。
我們的解決方案分為兩大產品組別：（1）智慧（Intelligence）與（2）啟動（Activation）。

•智慧產品包含跨通路測量、消費者行為與洞察以及零售商解決方案，被品牌與零售商客戶使用。這些產品協助客戶衡量其在各通路的消費購買市佔率，幫助他們瞭解 "什麼"、"在哪裡"、"誰" 以及 "多少"—消費者購買了什麼、消費者是誰、他們在哪裡購物以及他們購買了多少。客戶可以透過產品、市場與通路來觀察其市佔率，並觀察這些維度的銷售體積變動，以及價格與促銷趨勢。智慧產品在 2025 年 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度中，約佔本公司營業收入的 81%，通常透過多年或年度訂閱合約銷售。

•Activation offerings 包含創新、品牌與媒體及分析產品，提供客戶關於「為何」消費者做出特定購買的洞察，引導客戶在新產品推出與創新、定價、促銷策略、針對性廣告及其他成長驅動因素方面「應做何事」及「應針對誰」。透過我們高度細緻的統一資料與科技平台，我們的 Activation offerings 包含客製化、預測性分析與報告，客戶可用以優化品牌與通路決策以及新產品測試。Activation 在 2025 年 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度中，約佔本公司營業收入的 19%。在 2025 年 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度中，約 73% 的 Activation 營業收入為高度重複性收入，意指來自年度、多年度合約或來自客戶在過去三年內每年於相同國家購買相同解決方案的收入。Activation 解決方案也提供顯著的交叉銷售機會，因為在 2025 年 12 月 31 日為止的會計年度中，約 78% 的 Activation 營業收入來自於現有 Intelligence 客戶，而約 40% 的本公司 Intelligence 大型及中型客戶已購買 Activation 解決方案，代表增加市場佔有率的有吸引力機會。
我們的資料規模、廣度與深度，結合我們深厚的產業知識、可擴展的 AI 系統科技平台與強大的全球關係，使我們能為品牌、零售商、其他公司及政府機構提供相關解決方案。我們的客戶羣約為 23,000 家公司，橫跨產業與地理區域。我們與許多全球最大的消費品牌與零售商合作 – 包括約半數的財富 500 大企業與近 80% 的財富 100 大企業 – 以及高成長產業與中小企業客戶。
我們的解決方案使執行長、銷售主管、行銷人員、類別管理團隊、媒體主管及研究與開發團隊得以推動客戶企業的關鍵戰略與運營決策，包括：
•衡量與評估跨通路銷售表現，以瞭解哪些產品被銷售、誰購買、為何購買、何處購買及如何購買；
•優化定價與促銷，以評估對銷售的影響；
•區分與個人化消費者產品與體驗，以提高跨通路銷售轉換率與重複購買。

paragraphs: 於 2025 年 7 月 22 日，重組完成，NIQ Global Intelligence plc 成為 AI PAVE 的直接母公司，並間接成為其他間接控股公司的母公司，包括於荷蘭根據該國法律設立的私人有限公司，具有有限責任的 Intermediate Dutch Holdings B.V.（"Dutch Holdings"）。AI PAVE 所有權益持有人成為 NIQ Global Intelligence plc 的股東。
於 2025 年 7 月 24 日，我們完成首次公開發行股票（IPO），發行並出售 50,000,000 張普通股，每股發行價格為 21.00 美元。扣除經紀人折扣與佣金及預估發行費用後，我們收到總計 985.1 百萬美元的淨資金。總計淨資金用於償還本公司部分現有貸款。有關更多資訊，請參閱我們合併財務報表附註的第 1 註："組織" 以及第 10 註："債務"。

於 2025 年 7 月 11 日，信用協議經修改，以 IPO 關閉為前提，修改內容包括（i）將循環信貸（Revolver）總本金金額提高至 750.0 百萬美元，（ii）將循環信貸的到期日延長至 2030 年 7 月 30 日；但若於修改到期日（如後文所定義）之前，根據信用協議所借入的任何定期貸款總本金金額超過 1.0 十億美元，且該定期貸款的到期日早於 2030 年 7 月 30 日後 90 天的日期（"觸發到期日"），則該到期日應為觸發到期日往前 91 天的日期（"修改到期日"），（iii）將循環信貸設施的利率 spreads 減少至根據某些比率水平而定的 225 到 275 基點，（iv）將循環信貸的承諾費用率減少至根據某些比率水平而定的 25 到 37.5 基點。

於 2025 年 8 月 12 日，信用協議經修改，修改內容包括（a）以利率 spreads 減少至根據某些比率水平而定的 225 到 250 基點的新 USD 定期貸款設施，取代現有 USD 定期貸款，（b）以利率 spreads 減少至根據某些比率水平而定的 275 到 300 基點的新 EUR 定期貸款設施，取代現有 EUR 定期貸款，（c）將 USD 與 EUR 定期貸款設施的到期日延長至 2030 年 10 月 31 日，（d）將循環信貸的利率 spreads 減少至根據某些比率水平而定的 175 到 225 基點。有關更多資訊，請參閱我們合併財務報表附註的第 10 註："債務"。

於 2025 年 4 月 21 日，我們完成 Gastrograph 收購，以現金支付 12.5 百萬美元作為對價，並根據某些營運資金調整。我們將此交易視為資產購入，因所取得資產的公允價值幾乎全部集中在 Gastrograph 的已開發技術，包括應用程式、模型及基礎資料庫。我們認為 Gastrograph 收購進一步強化我們的 AI 能力與競爭優勢，以提供消費者包裝商品公司 The Full ViewTM。
於 2025 年 7 月 10 日，我們與巴西的數據智能與市場分析公司 M-Trix 籤訂最終協議，以取得其 100% 股權。交易於 2025 年 8 月 1 日完成，總現金對價約為 340.0 百萬巴西雷亞爾（相當於約 54.2 百萬美元），根據常見的買方價格調整條款，其中僅 150.0 百萬巴西雷亞爾（相當於約 26.8 百萬美元）於交易完成時支付。

剩餘的 190.0 百萬巴西雷亞爾將按以下方式支付：（i）於交易完成後第一年支付 60.0 百萬巴西雷亞爾，（ii）於交易完成後第二年支付 60.0 百萬巴西雷亞爾，（iii）於交易完成後第三年支付 50.0 百萬巴西雷亞爾，（iv）於交易完成後第六年支付 20.0 百萬巴西雷亞爾，但需符合 M-Trix 被要求賠償的任何持續主張。僅 Holdback Amount 會根據巴西的銀行存款證（"CDI"）進行調整。
與取得 M-Trix 有關，我們於 2025 年 7 月 28 日與 Banco J.P. Morgan S.A. 籤訂信用協議，以取得 150.0 百萬巴西雷亞爾（相當於約 26.8 百萬美元）用以資助交易。BRL 貸款的利率為 CDI 率加上 280 基點。我們於 2025 年第三季償還 BRL 貸款，包括累計利息。
本公司認為此次收購將擴大我們在拉丁美洲的業務版圖，並允許對現有產品進行升級。此次收購以收購法則會計處理為企業合併。請參閱我們合併財務報表附註第 3 項「收購」，以取得更多資訊。

headings: 與本公司業務及營運相關之風險
1. 我們從訂閱制產品之銷售中獲取相當大比例之營業收入。若客戶終止或未續訂其訂閱，本公司業務可能受影響。
4. 若我們無法維持足夠規模與範圍之消費者樣本組，或建立及維護樣本組之成本增加，本公司業務可能受損害。
5. 若我們未能投資於成長機會，本公司業務可能受到重大且不利之影響。
6. 總體經濟因素可能持續對本公司業務及財務結果造成不利影響。
7. 消費者測量及企業解決方案產品與服務之市場競爭激烈；若我們無法有效競爭，本公司收入可能下降，業務可能受損害。
8. 本公司客戶所屬產業之整併可能對我們服務之價格造成壓力，進而導致獲利與現金流減少。
9. 若資訊來源限制我們取得該資訊之權限，或提高取得該資訊之費用，本公司業務可能受到重大且不利之損害。
10. 若我們最大客戶之一發生虧損或業務減少，可能對我們的業務、營運結果及財務狀況造成不利影響。
11. 我們面臨向政府機構銷售的相關風險。
12. 我們成功管理持續的組織變革與成長的能力，可能影響我們的業務結果。
13. 我們可能無法完全實現已完成或未來合併、收購、合作投資及戰略投資的預期效益，這可能會使我們面臨額外風險。
14. 若我們無法吸引、留住並有效運用員工，我們可能無法有效競爭，也無法擴展業務。
15. 我們的保險覆蓋不足或無法取得契約所要求的保險，可能對我們的業務造成不利影響。
16. 自然災害、地緣政治事件及其他高度幹擾性的事件，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果造成重大且不利的影響。
17. 因為我們通常會根據每份訂閱協議的期限，按比例確認收入，因此我們銷售的上漲或下跌，可能不會立即反映在財務狀況及營運結果上。

paragraphs: 投資本公司的普通股涉及高度風險。您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險與不確定性，並配合本年度10-K形式年度報告中所有其他資訊，包括我們的合併財務報表及相關附註，再決定是否投資本公司的普通股。若下列任何風險發生，將可能對本公司業務、前景、營運結果與財務狀況造成重大影響，本公司普通股的交易價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。下列所描述的風險與不確定性並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，我們可能尚未知悉，或目前認為不具重大性，但這些風險與不確定性可能成為影響本公司業務的重要因素。
目前，我們的收入有相當大一部分來自長期訂閱合約，這些合約通常為兩至五年。這通常使我們獲得具有重複性收入，因客戶的續約率很高，如我們的淨美元保留率所顯示。若客戶終止訂閱我們的產品、不續約、延後續約或續約條件較不利於我們，則我們的收入可能下降，業務也可能受影響。

我們的客戶在初始訂閱期滿後，沒有義務續約，且目前的訂閱可能不會以相同或更高的金額續約，甚至可能完全不續約。客戶的續約率可能下降或波動，原因包括客戶對我們產品的不滿意、產品的成本或功能、競爭對手產品的價格或功能、消費者數據測量市場的健康狀況及我們所從事產業的情況、影響客戶羣的併購活動，以及總體經濟狀況或客戶減少支出水平。若客戶不續約、要求價格讓步、終止協議、以較不利於我們的條件續約或未能取得額外的產品訂閱，我們的收入可能下降，因此可能對我們的業務、營運結果與財務狀況造成不利影響。

此外，隨著我們的產品不斷演進，競爭對手可能推出成本較低或功能不同的產品，這些產品被視為與我們的產品和服務競爭，這可能影響我們取得產品訂閱的能力。同樣地，若客戶認為競爭產品的特點降低了對我們產品的需求，或他們更傾向於購買由其他公司提供的產品組合，而這些公司經營的市場與我們的產品相鄰且與我們的產品競爭，則我們的訂閱收入可能受到不利影響。此外，我們的產品和服務對客戶的價值，在一定程度上取決於客戶能否將其作為整體有效行銷策略的一部分，並符合有關數據主體同意的規範所允許的範圍。
2. 我們依賴第三方提供部分數據、服務與資訊科技及營運功能，以配合我們目前產品與服務的提供。若失去或無法取得這些數據、服務或功能，將可能影響我們提供產品與服務的能力。

我們依賴第三方，包括零售商、受測者及其他第三方，提供數據、服務與資訊科技及營運功能，以配合我們目前產品與服務的提供，且我們對第三方供應商的依賴正在增加。例如，我們與第三方簽訂協議以取得用來創造產品與服務的數據，並招募受測者以提供用來創造產品與服務的數據。我們也透過數據共享安排從可能與我們競爭的公司取得部分數據。這些數據供應商可能因提高的消費者隱私權規範、網路安全風險或未能遵守我們或他們的品質控制標準，或未能妥善執行服務等因素，而增加對我們使用這些數據的限制。第三方數據供應商也可能提高他們對數據收費的價格，或改變提供數據的條件，甚至完全拒絕授權我們使用這些數據（在某些情況下，這是因為他們與我們的競爭對手簽訂了獨佔協議）。若這些數據與服務無法供我們使用，或取得這些數據的成本增加，或這些第三方數據供應商拒絕提供數據，或未能將數據交付給我們，我們提供產品與服務給客戶的能力可能受到不利影響，因此可能對我們的業務、營運結果與財務狀況造成不利影響。
